title: The five Takhts
hook: the Ardas remembers the five seats of authority and all gurdwaras

segments.voice: Yesterday: morcha, and your line: they kept the doors, held open in the 1920s. Today the Ardas puts five pins in a map.

Draw a map of India and put five pins in it. Two in Punjab, close together. One more in Punjab, farther south. One way out east, on the Ganges, in Bihar. And one deep in the south-center of the country, in Maharashtra, far from all the others. These five pins aren't simply big gurdwaras. They're places where the community's authority sits, and the Ardas names them, as a group, every time it's prayed.
screen: `FIVE PINS IN A MAP OF INDIA.` → `PUNJAB, BIHAR, MAHARASHTRA.` → `WHERE AUTHORITY SITS.`

segments.voice: After the martyrs, the Ardas says: panjaan takhtaan, sarbatt gurduaariaan daa dhiaan dhar ke. Fixing the mind on the five Takhts and all the gurdwaras, say Waheguru. Takht means a throne, the seat of a ruler. A gurdwara is a house of the Guru, where the sangat prays. A Takht is a seat of authority, where decisions for the whole community are made and announced. One is the Akal Takht, the Throne of the Timeless, which Guru Hargobind, the Guru of the two swords, built facing the Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar. Edicts called hukamnamas, binding on Sikhs everywhere, are issued from there. The other four are tied to the life of Guru Gobind Singh. Takht Sri Patna Sahib, in Bihar, marks where he was born. Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib, at Anandpur, marks where he founded the Khalsa. Takht Sri Damdama Sahib, at Talwandi Sabo in southern Punjab, is where tradition says he stayed for a time and a final edition of the scripture was prepared. And Takht Sri Hazur Sahib, at Nanded in Maharashtra, marks where he died. Then the Ardas widens out: sarbatt gurduaariaan, all the gurdwaras. Every one, from the Harmandir to a rented hall above a shop. Five seats of authority, and every house of the Guru: all held in mind in one breath.
screen: `TAKHT: A THRONE, A SEAT.` · `THE AKAL TAKHT, AMRITSAR.` · `FOUR SEATS FROM THE TENTH GURU'S LIFE.` · `AND ALL THE GURDWARAS.` · then, large: `FIVE SEATS.`

segments.voice: Go through the five slowly in your mind: Akal Takht, Amritsar; Kesgarh Sahib, Anandpur; Damdama Sahib, Talwandi Sabo; Patna Sahib, Bihar; Hazur Sahib, Nanded. Pick one and picture it, the dome, the pilgrims, the morning light, then widen out to every gurdwara, including the one nearest you. If you pray, say Waheguru.
Takht. A throne, a seat of authority: the Akal Takht and four seats from the life of Guru Gobind Singh.
Your line: five seats. One for the Timeless, four from the tenth Guru's life. Day six hundred twenty-six, done.

chat.says: Is a Takht just a really big gurdwara?
options: Not quite: a Takht is a seat of authority, where decisions for the whole community are made.
Yes: Takht is simply the name for the five largest gurdwaras anywhere in India.
No: a Takht is a royal palace where Sikh kings once held court and lived.
